clue.text: Costing the earth? Just the opposite

definitions.text: Costing the earth? Just the opposite

parts.words: Costing the earth? Just the opposite
parts.note: the reverse of hugely expensive is going for next to nothing, and the earth hint suggests soil or muck as the measure of worth

explanation.surface: A remark that something supposedly pricey is in fact a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Costing the earth' means very expensive; the opposite is extremely cheap, and the answer's first word is another word for earth, so the clue plays on both.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sold for almost nothing is said to be as cheap as muck, the opposite of a sky-high price.

clue.text: Lemur found in Indiana and Rhode Island

parts.note: Ind. is the traditional abbreviation for the US state of Indiana
RI is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A primate apparently discovered living in two American states.
explanation.definitionFit: The indri is the largest living species of lemur, native to Madagascar.

definitions.meaning: the highest singing part, as sung by a boy soprano
threefold, as in a triple amount

explanation.surface: A singer's voice apparently able to do triple the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's high singing voice is called this; as a verb or adjective it also means triple or threefold.

parts.note: reads as a casual exclamation of relief, but describes someone who is well now after illness and so better

explanation.surface: A satisfied exclamation once a problem has been fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound or patient that has recovered is well again, i.e. better after sickness.

clue.text: The last word one is going to say in Spain

definitions.text: The last word one is going to say in Spain

parts.words: The last word one is going to say in Spain
parts.note: the final word a departing person utters in Spanish is the farewell, said on going

explanation.surface: A grim-sounding remark about someone's final utterance while in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a dying person's last words; really it is simply the Spanish for goodbye, said by someone leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish speakers use this farewell when parting, the last word as they go.

parts.note: a kinsman from the rural provinces, unused to city ways; the question mark flags the playful definition

explanation.surface: A query about a family member who lives away from the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes an unsophisticated person from the provinces, literally a kinsman from rural parts.

parts.note: make-up read as constitution, what girls are made of according to the old nursery rhyme, rather than cosmetics

explanation.surface: A note about cosmetics worn by young women.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme says little girls are made of these things 'and all things nice'; 'make-up' means composition, not cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: In the traditional rhyme, these sweet ingredients are what little girls are made of.

clue.text: One inside hopes to get time off for it

definitions.text: One inside hopes to get time off for it

parts.words: One inside hopes to get time off for it
parts.note: one inside is a prisoner, who may have a sentence shortened for conduct that is well behaved

explanation.surface: Someone indoors wishing for a break from work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' is slang for in prison, and remission of sentence is earned by conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners can earn early release by keeping out of trouble during their sentence.

parts.note: chap here means a sore crack in the skin rather than a man, and the foot is where it appears

explanation.surface: A fellow walking somewhere rather than riding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chap' looks like a man; it is chapped skin, and these cold-induced sores often appear on toes.
explanation.definitionFit: This itchy swelling caused by cold is a kind of chapping, frequently on the toes.

definitions.meaning: a layer of plaster applied to a wall

explanation.surface: Someone supplying a wall with plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means giving or supplying, and is also the builder's term for a first layer of plaster or cement on a wall.

indicators.note: signals that the letters sit within the words North India that follow

explanation.surface: A language spoken in the north of India.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the most widely spoken tongue of northern India and an official language there.

definitions.meaning: a sequence of musical notes in order of pitch

explanation.surface: Some musical notes rise in pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical run of successive notes is this; as a verb it means climb, as up a wall.

clue.text: The man, another day, was impetuous

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'The man, another day, was impetuous' (5) for HEADY: HE (the man) leaves ADY, and no reading of 'another day' gives those letters; likely an OCR or transcription error not resolvable from a search.
annotationWithheld.clue: The man, another day, was impetuous

clue.text: Used by those dyeing to be attractive

definitions.text: Used by those dyeing to be attractive

parts.words: Used by those dyeing to be attractive
parts.note: dyeing sounds like dying, so the surface suggests people desperate to look good, but it is a colouring agent for hair

explanation.surface: Something used by people desperate to look attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: This reddish plant dye is applied to hair and skin for cosmetic colouring.

indicators.note: the word is lies inside the drink, which wraps around it

parts.note: ale is a drink, a type of beer

explanation.surface: A corridor flooded with beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkway between rows of seats, as in a church or cinema.

indicators.note: a messy arrangement is a jumbled one, so the letters of as yet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that some fermenting agent is still making a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A fungus used in brewing and baking to ferment sugars.

indicators.note: over can mean upset or knocked over, so the letters are rearranged
except signals that something is taken away from the word all
leading points to the front letter of lady

explanation.surface: Someone enthusing about grubs, with the leading lady left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except leading lady' removes L from ALL, leaving AL; 'over' then rearranges AL plus RAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Insect young in their grub stage are larvae.

clue.text: Short journey made by king to S African ridge

parts.note: ER, from the Latin rex with et, is a regnal abbreviation; here king (Edwardus Rex)
the Rand, or Witwatersrand, is a gold-bearing ridge in South Africa

explanation.surface: A trip taken by a monarch to a South African range.
explanation.definitionFit: A short trip to do a task, such as fetching shopping.

indicators.note: turned round, so the letters of sent are rearranged

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A girl dispatched on a circuit carrying an item.
explanation.definitionFit: Nesta is a Welsh female name.

clue.text: Said to draw a comparison with a compound plant

indicators.note: spoken, so the word meaning compare is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to liken is to compare one thing with another

explanation.surface: A botanist comparing something with a plant made of several parts.
explanation.walkthrough: One common pronunciation of this organism matches the verb meaning compare.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a composite organism, a fungus living in partnership with an alga.

indicators.note: I is told to go away, so that letter departs from the serviceman

parts.note: a soldier is a serviceman in the army

explanation.surface: A soldier going on leave to join up.
explanation.definitionFit: To fuse metal parts together with molten alloy, uniting them.

parts.note: dept is the short form of department

explanation.surface: A specialist working in a little office section.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilled and proficient is adept, a synonym of expert.

explanation.surface: Someone stooping twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means two-fold, and also folded or stooped, as in being doubled up with laughter.

explanation.surface: Someone seeking a reason for being let off.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means forgive; as a noun it is the official cancelling of a penalty.

clue.text: Get used to being in the river

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Advice to acclimatise yourself to swimming.
explanation.definitionFit: To accustom or harden someone to something unpleasant.

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of they are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Some chemical that people left lying around.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydrocarbon group found in alcohol and other organic compounds.

definitions.meaning: with a hat on, so wearing only part of an outfit
a castrated domestic cock reared for eating

explanation.surface: A bird with only some of its clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as two words it means wearing a hat, partial attire; as one word it is a castrated cockerel fattened for the table.

clue.text: Vandalised a cart worth its weight in gold

indicators.note: something vandalised is wrecked, so the letters of a cart are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A precious cart that someone has smashed up.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit expressing the purity of gold, out of twenty-four parts, or a gemstone's weight.

clue.text: Unwillingly accompanying a naughty girl, it appears

parts.note: with means accompanying, along with
bad means naughty, as of a child
Grace is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Reluctantly going along with a misbehaving young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something grudgingly, showing resentment and reluctance.

clue.text: Every second bird in a new tale

indicators.note: the bird sits inside the reworked letters
new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of a tale

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A bird appears in every second instalment of a fresh story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every second' looks like a time phrase but is the definition, as in every second day; 'new' is the anagram signal sitting between its two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurring on every other one, as in alternate days.
